title: Spec and fix the video recorder's refused-camera-access message on macOS and Android

completion_criteria.text: macOS: after the camera prompt is refused, the video recorder shows cameraPermissionMessage, not videoDeviceListMessage.
completion_criteria.check: A widget test whose camera_macos channel fake returns the plugin's real refusal reply {"error": {"code": "CAMERA_INITIALIZATION_ERROR", "message": "Permission not granted"}} fails before the fix and passes after; live in the reverted clean Parallels guest, a fresh .plain install pressing Don't Allow on the camera prompt shows the permission message.

completion_criteria.text: Android: after the camera or microphone prompt is refused, the video recorder shows cameraPermissionMessage straight away, instead of a blank Ready to record followed by videoStartMessage on Start.
completion_criteria.check: A widget test faking CameraException('CameraAccessDenied') and CameraException('AudioAccessDenied') from camera start-up fails before the fix and passes after; live on the Note10+ with a .plain debug build, Don't allow on both prompts shows the permission message before Start.

completion_criteria.text: The allowed paths are unchanged: a Mac with no camera still says videoDeviceListMessage and keeps it when Start is pressed, and recording still works on the owner's Mac and on the Note10+ when access is allowed.
completion_criteria.check: The existing no_camera_test.dart tests still pass; live, the guest's allowed-no-camera path shows 'Could not find a camera' with 0 changed pixels after Start, and a short recording saves on the Note10+.

completion_criteria.text: The whole suite and analyzer are clean on the merged result.
completion_criteria.check: flutter test (run per top-level test folder) passes and flutter analyze reports no issues.

open_risks.text: macOS root cause, confirmed by code and live: the vendored camera_macos plugin never sends a refusal as a platform error. Swift listDevices calls requestPermission (video only) and, when refused, replies result(FlutterError(code: "CAMERA_INITIALIZATION_ERROR", message: "Permission not granted").toFlutterResult), which is the success value {"error": {code, message, details}} (CameraMacosPlugin.swift ~265, FlutterMacOS+Extension.swift). Its Dart listDevices finds no "devices" key and throws FlutterError("Invalid args: invalid platform response") (camera_macos_method_channel.dart ~41). The app's new branch in CameraMacosVideoRecorder.listDevices (camera_video_recorder.dart ~424) only matches `on PlatformException` with message 'Permission not granted', so the catch-all shows videoDeviceListMessage. The merged test passed only because it fakes a PlatformException (no_camera_test.dart ~99-103). Live: clean guest, fresh install, Don't Allow on the camera prompt gave 'Could not find a camera. Connect one and try again.'

macOS fix-site choice for the spec: (a) recommended, since the plugin is vendored: make its Dart listDevices (and the other methods that `throw result["error"]` as a raw Map at camera_macos_method_channel.dart ~116, 154, 198) turn an {"error": {...}} reply into PlatformException(code, message, details); the app branch then works unchanged. (b) App-side: also catch FlutterError whose message is 'Invalid args: invalid platform response'. That is fragile, because the same message covers any malformed reply. Whichever is chosen, the acceptance test must fake the channel's real reply map, not a PlatformException.

Android root cause, confirmed live and by code: availableCameras() works without permission, so listDevices succeeds and the composer goes idle ('Tap when you’re ready', blank preview). The refusal only surfaces inside CameraVideoRecorder._initialise (camera_video_recorder.dart ~280-307), where controller.initialize() throws CameraException('CameraAccessDenied' or 'AudioAccessDenied', from camera_android_camerax 0.7.4+2 CameraPermissionsManager.java) and the catch-all wraps it as VideoRecorderException(videoStartMessage). That failure sits in the session's ready future and is only seen when Start awaits it, giving 'Could not start recording. Check your camera and try again.' The fix needs two parts: map those CameraException codes to cameraPermissionMessage, and surface a session start-up failure to the composer as the denied state at once. VideoRecorder.openSession returns only a Widget today, so the second part is an interface change touching both recorders and every fake recorder in the tests.

Unverified: what macOS does when camera is allowed but the microphone is refused. The vendored plugin's requestPermission asks for video only, and the guest run never showed a microphone prompt. cameraPermissionMessage names both camera and microphone. Check it live on the host or guest before the spec fixes the wording or the refusal set.
